prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and dynamics of a mass point, Newton's axioms, forces, impulse, angular momentum, work, power, energy, conservation laws)
Knowledge of static fluids (pressure distribution and hydrostatic pressure, density and specific weight, buoyancy)
Elementary fluid dynamics (continuity equation, flow types, pressure distribution in flowing fluids, viscosity and friction, gravity and buoyancy forces)
Optics (geometric optics, light as electromagnetic wave, reflection, refraction and dispersion)
Knowledge of thermodynamics (basic concepts, ideal gases, main laws of thermodynamics, cyclic processes, real gases, phase transitions)
Basics of heat transfer (heat conduction, convection, thermal radiation)

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basics of the supply and usability of renewable energies in the field of solar and geothermal energy.
They understand the essential principles of the physical-technical aspects of solar and geothermal energy use.
Students know the essential principles of the application areas and dimensioning of corresponding systems.
They have acquired practical skills in creating solar thermal simulation models and can analyze their results.

syllabus_topics: Heating energy demand in residential buildings
Solar thermal use of renewable energies in the low and high temperature range (including domestic hot water heating and heating support, swimming pool heating, solar thermal power plants)
Geothermal use. Functioning of the heat pump (geothermal heating and cooling)

Internship (e.g., experiments and simulations for dimensioning solar thermal systems for domestic hot water and swimming pool heating, and for the functioning and determination of the performance coefficients of a heat pump)

assessment_methods.method: Written exam or oral examination (Klausur oder mündliche Prüfung)

assessment_rules: To receive credit points, the module examination must be passed, including a preliminary coursework.
